executive_summary: Your printing substrates and nicotine supply chains are concentrated in geopolitically volatile regions—Finland (NATO border), China (trade war/Taiwan), and South Africa (infrastructure crisis)—creating overlapping rather than diversified risk. More urgent is your critical dependency on two Chinese EMS suppliers (Huizhou BYD, Smoore) and one German semiconductor player (Infineon) facing an unexplained 8.7% stock crash; Infineon's collapse is the immediate outlier and warrants a direct vendor call within 24 hours to rule out production or solvency issues. The China nexus deserves consolidated attention: four suppliers across EMS, batteries, and nicotine are all exposed to the same US-China trade and Taiwan scenarios, so a single policy shift or geopolitical event could cascade across multiple categories. South Africa's energy crisis affecting Sappi and India's border tensions affecting ITC are secondary in urgency but worth mapping as secondary sources in case Chinese suppliers tighten. Start with Infineon clarification, then pressure test your China supplier redundancy.
